title: Meeting-to-Deep-Work Ratio
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports (`calendar:event`), email metadata (`email:metadata`), password-audit reports (`passwordmanager:audit`).
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, password-audit exports, and calendar/email feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:event
| bin _time span=1w
| stats sum(eval(if(category="meeting",duration_min,0))) as meeting_min, sum(eval(if(category="focus",duration_min,0))) as focus_min by _time
| eval ratio=if(focus_min=0,meeting_min,round(meeting_min/focus_min,2))
| where meeting_min>0
| sort - ratio
description: Compares weekly meeting time with explicitly protected deep-work time, making the trade-off between collaboration and concentration impossible to hand-wave.
value: A ratio is easy to track and discuss with yourself; it tells you whether your calendar design still matches the kind of work you want to do.
implementation: Forward calendar events categorized by meeting versus focus; review the ratio weekly and reset next week's schedule before drift compounds.
visualization: Weekly chart of meeting minutes, focus minutes, and their ratio.
grandmaExplanation: It measures how much of your week is going to meetings compared with real focused work time.
